tool: Phase 3D validation protocol V2 (candidate): separation of production reproduction, deterministic agreement, orientation-aligned simulation agreement and native-orientation Monte Carlo agreement
status_of_this_document: CANDIDATE. Declared before any V2 study run. V2 is a REVISION introduced AFTER the orientation investigation; it does not replace, edit or re-grade V1. The V1 protocol (config/dlm_validation_protocol.json, hash REDACTED_PUBLIC_BUILD), the V1 reference plan (config/validation_plan_dlm.json, hash REDACTED_PUBLIC_BUILD), the simulation-diagnostic protocol (config/dlm_simulation_diagnostic_protocol.json, hash REDACTED_PUBLIC_BUILD), all V1 reports and the recorded statuses of dlmvalidate_20261002_163715_0c0b (REFERENCE_COMPARISON = FAIL, SIMULTANEOUS_EXACT_SEEDED = FAIL) are preserved unchanged.

introduced_after.reason: V1 required exact seeded agreement (1e-9) of simultaneous critical values between implementations. The manual V1 run showed that this requirement fails for reasons that are not errors of fitting, covariance or sampling.

evidence.finding: reference comparison FAIL (4 critical values, 0.09% to 0.42%) and exact-seeded FAIL (3 cross-implementation checks); fitted quantities, p values, q9, peaks and band conclusions unaffected
diagnostic built with declared methods and allowance before execution

run dlmsimdiag_20261002_174941_1241: production replica bitwise (18/18); all factors reconstruct; all six production cross-route discrepancies explained by the sign of 4 of 27 eigenvectors (lag-space cosine -1); aligned agreement 1e-7 or better in 18/18; all four reference mismatches reproduced by a sign pattern of the production factor (compatible, not proof of the historical engine's behaviour)

what_V2_does_not_claim: that V1 was wrong or that its FAIL statuses are cancelled (they remain recorded as FAIL under the V1 criteria)
exact reproduction of the historical (legacy) engine's simulation
validity of a reference value because some sign pattern reproduces it

unchanged_numbers: No numerical tolerance and no Monte Carlo criterion is loosened or changed. V2 reads every number from the V1 protocol (config/dlm_validation_protocol.json): fitted-quantity tolerances 1e-8 abs + 1e-7 rel (binary at the accepted epsilon 1e-6 + 1e-6, tight-epsilon check 1e-8 + 1e-7), existing named tolerance sets of the configuration, Monte Carlo stability (20 alternative seeds, 100,000-draw value, seeded value within 5% of it, spread at most 0.2, identical band-exclusion counts), cross-implementation Monte Carlo bound 5% with identical exclusion counts, and the declared covariance allowance of the diagnostic protocol. The tests assert this equality.

A_production_reproduction.question: Does unchanged code on the same data and configuration with the same RNG settings reproduce the accepted fits and the production simulation?
A_production_reproduction.required_evidence: accepted-run tables (9 summaries, 504 lag rows, 504 cumulative rows) equal within the existing exact class (1e-12); the diagnostic's replica of the production draws and critical values bitwise equal for all nine models at 5,000 and 10,000 draws; RNG metadata recorded
A_production_reproduction.failure_means: fitting, data, configuration or sampling reproduction failure

B_deterministic_agreement.question: Do the independent route and the package agree on everything that does not involve random draws?
B_deterministic_agreement.required_evidence: lag basis; coefficients (lag effects); lag SEs; pointwise bands; cumulative effects, SEs and bands; peak lags; global statistics and p values; q9 (BH of the independent p values equals the package q9); the band formula with the package critical value and the band-exclusion counts; binary models also at epsilon 1e-14; lag-space covariance on the standard-deviation scale
B_deterministic_agreement.tolerances: existing V1 fitted-quantity tolerances; covariance is judged on the standard-deviation scale: half of the largest relative difference of the lag-space covariance (the first-order equivalent of a relative standard-deviation difference) must not exceed the existing relative fitted-quantity tolerance (1e-7; 1e-6 for binary models at the accepted epsilon); this restates the existing SE tolerance for a covariance matrix and adds no looser value

C_orientation_aligned_simulation.question: With identical standard normals and a documented deterministic sign convention in lag space, do the two implementations produce the same simulated critical values?
C_orientation_aligned_simulation.sign_convention: each eigenvector v of the coefficient covariance is oriented so that the component of B v (B = lag basis) with the largest absolute value is positive; B v is coordinate free, so both implementations apply the same convention
C_orientation_aligned_simulation.required_evidence: identical standard normals (the independent clone's draws and the production draws are both reproduced bitwise from the same matrix); every factor reconstructs its covariance (1e-12); aligned-eigen critical values of the two routes agree within the declared covariance allowance max(1e-9, 10 x lag-space relative covariance difference x critical value) at 5,000 and 10,000 draws; every production cross-route difference beyond the allowance is explained (flipping the lag-space cosine -1 components of the independent factor reproduces the production value within the allowance)
C_orientation_aligned_simulation.failure_means: sampling failure, covariance/factor reconstruction failure, or UNRESOLVED ORIENTATION (a difference that orientation does not explain, including components whose lag-space cosine is neither +1 nor -1)

D_native_orientation_monte_carlo_agreeme.question: With each implementation's own eigenvector signs, are the simulated critical values Monte Carlo consistent and are the band conclusions stable?
D_native_orientation_monte_carlo_agreeme.criteria: the V1 Monte Carlo stability criteria, unchanged (per model: seeded 5,000-draw value within 5% of the 100,000-draw value; spread across 20 alternative seeds at most 0.2; identical number of lags excluding zero for the seeded value, every alternative seed, the 100,000-draw value, the independent-route value and, at the audited draw count, the reference), plus the V1 cross-implementation class (EXACT or MC_CONSISTENT_NOT_EXACT within 5% with identical exclusion counts)
D_native_orientation_monte_carlo_agreeme.exact_differences: remain visible in dlm_v2_exact_differences_visible.csv with their V1 band and orientation explanation; an exact difference is NOT the cross-implementation acceptance requirement
D_native_orientation_monte_carlo_agreeme.failure_means: stability failure (including threshold sensitivity of a band conclusion)

reconstructed_reference.deterministic_comparisons: REFERENCE_DETERMINISTIC: estimates (n, global statistic, p, q9, cumulative effect, SE and interval, peak effect) at the existing dlm tolerance, and peak lag and band-exclusion counts exact: required, unchanged from V1
reconstructed_reference.simulated_critical_values: REFERENCE_SIMULATION_MC: the audited critical value at 10,000 draws is assessed with the declared Monte Carlo criterion (relative difference from the production value at 10,000 draws within 5%, band-exclusion counts identical) - not with the 1e-9 exact-seeded class
reconstructed_reference.preserved: the exact differences, their V1 class (EXACT / NEAR_EXACT / REALISATION_DIFFERENCE) and the orientation explanation (sign pattern of the production factor that reproduces the reference value) are saved for every model
reconstructed_reference.limits: a sign pattern that reproduces a reference value shows compatibility with an orientation variant of the same simulation; it is annotation only and is never the basis of validity and never evidence of the historical engine's behaviour

statuses.v1_record_note: the nested V1 component is computed in this run with the unchanged V1 criteria and printed for the record; it does not decide V2 acceptance
statuses.rule: NOT_TESTED is never PASS. A required status FAILS on any genuine fitting, covariance, sampling, unresolved-orientation or stability failure.
statuses.exit_codes: 0 every status PASS; 3 every required status PASS while a separately reported status is REVIEW or NOT_TESTED (documented); 4 a required status FAILED; 1 execution failure; 2 invalid arguments
